The Facilities & HSE Officer – Automotive oversees daily maintenance, physical security, and environmental health and safety compliance across automotive facilities (dealership showrooms, service workshops, body shops, and spare parts warehouses). This role manages facility uptime, HVAC and shop equipment operations, hazardous material storage, workshop environmental compliance, and safety auditing. The primary objective is to maintain a high-standard, operational, safe, and fully compliant workplace for technicians, showroom staff, and customers.
q: Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Engineering (Mechanical or Electrical), Environmental Health & Safety (EHS), or related technical fields.
NEBOSH IGC or OSHA 30-hour certification required. Valid First Aid/CPR and Fire Warden certifications.
Familiarity with ISO 14001 (Environmental) and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety) standards.
5–7 years of hands-on experience in property maintenance, contractor oversight, and health & safety enforcement in corporate, commercial, or automotive multi-site settings.

Sound knowledge of civil, electrical, and mechanical infrastructure; expertise in life-safety systems (CCTV, fire alarms, sprinklers); proficiency in hazardous material/waste management and risk assessments (JSA).
Proven track record in evaluating contractors, negotiating SLAs for cost efficiency, overseeing cleaning/security operations, and coordinating office onboarding logistics.
Strong leadership and communication skills, decisive crisis management during operational disruptions or safety incidents, and meticulous record-keeping abilities.
r: Oversee and resolve all operational, structural, and infrastructure issues across company premises.
Conduct frequent physical inspections of properties to identify operational defects, managing and executing mechanical, electrical, and civil works requested by General Managers.
Analyze, scope, and process approvals for civil, mechanical, and electrical requests across divisions before execution.

Inspect, maintain, and ensure the full operational readiness of all life-safety and security systems, including CCTV, fire alarms, fire hose reels, smoke sensors, heat detectors, and water sprinklers.
Identify technical issues with life-safety equipment and liaise with specialized fire safety contractors (such as Alpha Fire Co. or Gulf Services Co.) for prompt rectification.
Develop, test, and maintain operational contingency plans to mitigate business disruptions and safeguard daily continuity.
Coordinate with Group HSE & Admin personnel to oversee concurrent multi-site projects and vendor activities without interrupting core business operations.
Coordinate with all external suppliers, contractors, and service providers to ensure deliverables meet contractual standards and organizational requirements.
Negotiate service terms with contractors, maintenance firms, and suppliers to secure competitive pricing, high quality, and economies of scale.
Conduct timely supplier evaluations for all maintenance service providers across divisions to ensure performance compliance.
Supervise fire protection contractors, verifying that all works comply with approved technical specifications and that Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs) are renewed on schedule.
Manage the commercial approval process and legal formalities for the disposal and sale of scrap materials.
Supervise security personnel across all corporate sites to ensure property protection and access control.
Manage direct line supervision over maintenance and janitorial staff across company properties.
Enforce cleaning, hygiene, and aesthetic standards across all premises to maintain corporate brand uniformity.
Provision and arrange all necessary logistical support, office furniture, and workstations for new hires based on HR notifications and department requirements.
Ensure full organizational compliance with all local HSE laws, regulatory standards, and internal safety protocols.
Maintain comprehensive records of all workplace HSE incidents, forwarding detailed accident and near-miss reports to the Division General Manager, Group HR & Admin Manager, and Division HR.
Lead incident investigations as directed by leadership, conducting root-cause analyses and issuing corrective action plans.
Attend monthly executive management meetings, representing administrative operations and resolving department-specific challenges.
Execute special projects, strategic assignments, and operational tasks directed by the Managing Director, General Manager, or Group HR & Admin Manager.

Our ambition is to set a standard of excellence in the industry for technical documentation and documentation practice. This is your chance to be a part of that, as a Technical Author at Canonical.
p
We are building documentation capacity at scale. We have dozens of positions available, for teams and products across the organisation, at all levels from Graduate to Senior Staff.
h
All applications and candidates are handled through this one entry-point.
p
To improve your chances of success in this application, read our advice on how to get a job at Canonical.
p

These are not traditional technical writer roles. As a Technical Author, you will lead the documentation efforts of a Canonical team, in engineering, business operations or another part of the company.
p

You will combine excellence in technical communication with subject-matter expertise and the ability to collaborate with colleagues across the organisation. Even the most junior Technical Authors will have the opportunity to develop and demonstrate technical authority, contributing to documentation practice as a first-class engineering and business discipline.
p
You will work with the Diátaxis approach to documentation and help elevate standards of technical writing through attention to theory and practice.
h
The role of a Technical Author
p

A product-focused Technical Author is a member of a product engineering team, typically focused on a product or family of products. In this role you'll help the team develop documentation that serves the needs of the product's users. You will have responsibility for the quality of the user experience with the product, and will contribute towards the long-term success of the project itself.
p

A customer-focused Technical Author works in a team such as Field Engineering, Customer Success or Support, dealing with users of complex suites of Canonical software products, sometimes deployed in custom configurations. In this role you’ll take a responsive approach to software documentation problems and develop a strong understanding of how products work together and are used in the real world.
p

An operations-focused Technical Author is part of a business team, for example Legal, HR or Talent. An important part of this work is to maintain internal documentation, such as employee handbooks. In this role you will help develop and improve materials that hundreds of colleagues rely on daily, and define patterns of business communication for a rapidly-growing organisation.
p
Some open technical author roles at Canonical
p
You’ll have a chance to tell us your preferred focus, and we'll work with you to find the right seniority level and team for you.
p

Whatever your focus, you will also be a part of Canonical's documentation practice team, that includes all the company's Technical Authors. Here, you'll be amongst other documentation experts, who collaborate to define documentation excellence and drive the development of documentation practice and theory, across the company and in the open-source software community.
p
Location: These are fully remote roles, open to candidates across the globe.
r: Create, maintain and improve software and other documentation
Work with your team members, to help them make effective documentation contributions
Influence the development of Canonical products and services, as an expert user who has important opinions about function and design
Engage with user communities to ensure that our documentation meets their needs
Encourage and support community engagement in and contribution to documentation
Help standardise the structure, presentation, style and language of content across products
Collaborate with documentation peers to advance the state of the art in documentation at Canonical
Challenge and advance documentation understanding and best-practice, as part of a disciplinary team
Is an excellent collaborator and communicator
Cares deeply about functional written communication
Is a technical writer with a programmer’s mindset, or a programmer with a record of producing excellent documentation
Has a record of community engagement, in open-source software, documentation, research or other disciplines
Is sympathetic to the needs and challenges of open-source software and its communities
Demonstrates technical curiosity, and is fascinated by software technology and its challenges
Has demonstrable documentation skills, insight and enthusiasm
Has experience of software development contexts
Is familiar with: Linux, working on the command line, Git, Sphinx, reStructuredText
Holds a BSc/BA degree or equivalent
Is able to travel twice a year for up to two weeks for events
x: We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.
Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events
